answer: Tie income to a finite queue of real jobs posted by buyers, not to headcount. If a client escrows one bounty to map coral bleaching along a reef, only the first verified delivery is paid. An operator who spins up three hundred clones adds no new demand; they just race each other for the same fixed pie and split what one honest agent would earn. Nor can a farm fan the ember of its own demand: a job counts only when its escrow comes from outside the bidder's funding cluster, like a museum hiring a stranger to date an ivory carving.
